courses.name: B.Sc. in Computer Science
aliases: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
courses.summary: A B.Sc. in Computer Science is a science-faculty bachelor's degree in the theory and practice of computing. The curriculum covers programming, data structures and algorithms, discrete mathematics, computer architecture, operating systems, databases, networks and software engineering, with electives in artificial intelligence, data science, cyber security or graphics. It differs from a B.E./B.Tech by placing more weight on mathematics and computing theory and less on engineering design. Programmes last three or four years and lead to software, data and IT roles or to master's study.

universities.name: M.O.P. Vaishnav College for Women (Autonomous)
universities.summary: M.O.P. Vaishnav College for Women is an autonomous, self-financing college affiliated to the University of Madras in Nungambakkam, Chennai. Established in 1992, it offers study in commerce, business, computing, media, food science and social sciences. These undergraduate routes describe Indian women’s school-entry conditions and regular campus study.
universities.campusLifestyle: The central Chennai campus brings academic departments, library facilities, media and computing spaces, and student activities together. Programme shifts and practical work affect the daily timetable. The current handbook has dress, identity-card and classroom mobile-phone rules; review these before choosing a programme and commute.
universities.cityProfile: The college is at 20, IV Lane, Nungambakkam High Road, Chennai 600034. Its urban setting suits students planning a city commute. Confirm shift hours and travel arrangements before acceptance; the handbook has vehicle and parking rules, and private accommodation requires a separate arrangement.
universities.practicalExposure: Department curricula include subject-specific projects, practical work, field visits and internships. The college describes media studios, food-production facilities, computing resources and business-on-campus learning. The exact requirements vary by award; obtain the current curriculum, supervision arrangements and any materials or external-visit costs.
universities.hostelOverview: The current institutional MBA disclosure records no girls’ hostel seats, and the historical institutional report states the college does not operate a hostel. Applicants needing accommodation should obtain current college guidance and assess private housing separately. A programme offer does not include a residence place or establish its cost.
universities.dietarySupport: The 2025–26 handbook describes a college food court supplying vegetarian food and permits students to bring their own vegetarian food. It also describes Beyond Breads, a health cafeteria. Confirm current opening hours, menu, prices and any allergy requirements before budgeting; these services do not establish a residence meal plan.
universities.safetyOverview: The handbook describes in-campus medical support through Apollo Shine, accessible ramps, elevators and washrooms, and campus conduct rules. Obtain current emergency contacts and the procedure for medical help at induction. Confirm travel and private-housing arrangements separately from the college’s on-campus services.
universities.studentSupport: The college describes a campus counsellor available by appointment through its Happiness Centre, mentoring and counselling resources, and library/digital research facilities. Students receive an intranet account for academic information. Confirm current access and departmental support arrangements during induction.

faq.question: Who can apply through these undergraduate routes?
faq.answer: Indian women holding the accepted school qualification and meeting the exact subject conditions may apply. Qualification equivalence and any foreign-national route require a separate college assessment.

faq.question: Which university is the college affiliated to?
faq.answer: M.O.P. Vaishnav College for Women is an autonomous college affiliated to the University of Madras. Autonomous study still follows applicable degree and admission requirements.

faq.question: What first-year date is available?
faq.answer: The 2025–26 annual report records induction for the incoming 2025–2028 undergraduate cohort on 23–28 June 2025. That historical orientation baseline does not guarantee the next cohort’s class-start date.

faq.question: What is the teaching language?
faq.answer: The dated 2022 institutional programme table records English for these continued award/faculty routes. Language papers have their own subjects. The exact current department curriculum should be checked at admission.

faq.question: How much is undergraduate tuition?
faq.answer: Obtain a current official quotation for the exact undergraduate award and applicant category. Request tuition and compulsory academic charges separately for the exact programme and shift.

faq.question: Are there entrance or skill assessments?
faq.answer: Conditions vary by programme. Visual Communication uses assessment/evaluation; Electronic Media uses an entrance test and expects media, current-affairs and global-social-issue knowledge. Check the exact selected course instructions.

faq.question: How do I apply?
faq.answer: Use the college-linked admission portal for the current cycle, choose the exact programme and shift, and follow its qualifying-record, selection and verification steps. An application does not guarantee admission.

faq.question: Which documents are required?
faq.answer: Prepare qualifying marks and subject details, and obtain the exact identification, photo, original-record and category checklist from the current application form. Requirements for qualification equivalence must be assessed individually.

faq.question: Does the college provide a hostel?
faq.answer: The current institutional disclosure records no girls’ hostel seats, and the historical institutional report says the college does not operate a hostel. Seek current college guidance and arrange private accommodation independently.

faq.question: What food is available?
faq.answer: The handbook describes a vegetarian food court, permits students to bring vegetarian food, and lists a health cafeteria. Confirm current menu, prices, hours and dietary needs directly.

faq.question: What support services are described?
faq.answer: The handbook lists medical support, counselling by appointment, mentoring, accessible facilities and library/digital resources. Confirm current procedures and service availability at induction.

faq.question: What everyday rules should students check?
faq.answer: The handbook has dress, visible identity-card, classroom mobile-phone, vehicle and conduct rules. Check these alongside the exact shift timetable before arranging travel and accepting admission.
